title: Internal ambient adjunction
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. For a compactifiable morphism $f:X\to S$ between
Noetherian schemes, and arbitrary complexes $M$ on
$X$ and $K$ on $S$, there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K).
$$

The notation refers to derived pullback and internal Hom, and ordinary etale compact supports.

proof.text: Work throughout on small étale sites with the constant commutative coefficient ring $A$, in a universe in which the sites are small. For any scheme morphism $u$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies module pullback with exact $u^{-1}$ and supplies its adjunction to $u_*$. Its termwise localization exists by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Thus it is its everywhere-defined left derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Module sheaves have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to $Q u_*$ on the homotopy category: this functor is exact there since additive $u_*$ preserves the finite sums and differential matrices defining shifts and cones. Hence $Ru_*$ exists on the unbounded category and is computed on K-injectives. Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $N$ and a complex $T$ representing $Q$. The module adjunction applies degreewise to chain maps and to homotopies: a homotopy consists of maps $T^n\to u_*I^{n-1}$, whose adjoints satisfy the same equation $a-b=dh+hd$. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(V)}(T,u_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U)}(u^{-1}T,I)$. If $E$ is acyclic on $V$, exactness of $u^{-1}$ makes $u^{-1}E$ acyclic, so this equality makes every map $E\to u_*I$ null-homotopic. Thus $u_*I$ is K-injective. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to $u_*I$ and to $I$ now gives the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V)}(Q,Ru_*N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(V)}(T,u_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U)}(u^{-1}T,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U)}(u^{-1}Q,N)$. The adjunction and localization maps are natural; changing a K-injective representative uses the homotopy equivalences in the same cited lemma, so these bijections are independent of representatives. Denote this adjunction's counit by $\varepsilon_u$.

proof.text: For a small ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, arbitrary $B,C,D\in D(\mathcal O)$ satisfy the natural tensor–internal-Hom bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(B,R\mathcal Hom(C,D))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes^{L}C,D)$. Here is its deduction from the cited statements, rather than from a definition: choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective representative $I$ of $D$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and any representative $T$ of $B$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$ represents $R\mathcal Hom(C,D)$ and is K-injective. The natural chain isomorphism of [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] therefore identifies $R\mathcal Hom(B,R\mathcal Hom(C,D))$ with $R\mathcal Hom(B\otimes^{L}C,D)$: its two representatives are $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(T,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I))$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes P),I)$. Taking zeroth derived global sections and applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on both sides gives the asserted bijection. All the chain maps used are the natural currying maps; evaluation is the inverse image of the identity of the internal Hom.

Choose a compactification $f=rj$ as in [def-asd-compactifiable]. First prove the open projection formula $j_!M\otimes_A^L N\cong j_!(M\otimes_A^Lj^{-1}N)$ for arbitrary $M,N$. The slice of $\overline X_{\mathrm{et}}$ over the open scheme $X$ is $X_{\mathrm{et}}$: an object is precisely an étale scheme over $X$, and covering families are the same. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-exactness] apply to this $j_!$. Choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $P\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its restriction $j^{-1}P$ is K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], and computes $j^{-1}N$ since inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The sheaf-level tensor isomorphism, applied in every bidegree and totalized, gives $\operatorname{Tot}(j_!M^\bullet\otimes P)\cong j_!\operatorname{Tot}(M^\bullet\otimes j^{-1}P)$. Extension by zero commutes with the direct sums in this totalization because it is left adjoint to restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]: maps from either sum into any target are the same family of adjoint maps. Its exactness makes it preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so these complexes compute the desired derived formula. The comparison is natural, being induced by the natural sheaf-level tensor map.

The proper part $r:\overline X\to S$ is of finite type and quasi-compact, by the definition of proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $S$ is Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $\overline X$ locally Noetherian. It is quasi-compact: cover $S$ by finitely many affine opens, take finite affine covers of their inverse images using quasi-compactness of $r$, and combine these covers. Thus $\overline X$ is Noetherian, so the chosen compactification meets exactly the hypotheses of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Apply [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] to $L=j_!M$ and $Q\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Combine its isomorphism with step 3 and $Rf_!=Rr_*j_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] to obtain the natural isomorphism
$$\pi_{Q,M}:Q\otimes_A^LRf_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!(f^{-1}Q\otimes_A^LM).$$
Explicitly it is $Q\otimes Rr_*j_!M\to Rr_*(r^{-1}Q\otimes j_!M)\to Rr_*j_!(j^{-1}r^{-1}Q\otimes M)$. The identity $j^{-1}r^{-1}=f^{-1}$ is composition of inverse images: both functors are left adjoint to $r_*j_*=f_*$, and the canonical identification sends their counits to the composite counit. Tensor factors may be interchanged by the chain sign symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in degrees $(p,q)$; its inverse has the same formula and it commutes with the total differential.

source.place: Proof: third displayed bijection, proper projection formula preceded by extension by zero

proof.text:
Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K)$, $U=Rf_*H$ and $V=R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K)$. For every $Q\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, steps 1, 2 and 4, together with the exceptional adjunction of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], give
$$\begin{aligned}
\Phi_Q:\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q,U)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^{-1}Q,H)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^{-1}Q\otimes_A^LM,f^\times K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Rf_!(f^{-1}Q\otimes_A^LM),K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q\otimes_A^LRf_!M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q,V).
\end{aligned}$$
The fourth arrow is precomposition with $\pi_{Q,M}$; all arrows are bijective and natural in $Q,M,K$. No boundedness, constructibility or finite Tor amplitude of a test object or coefficient complex has been used.

source.place: Proof: full displayed chain of natural Hom bijections

proof.text:
Construct the required morphism explicitly: $\theta=\Phi_U(1_U):U\to V$ and $\psi=\Phi_V^{-1}(1_V):V\to U$. Naturality in $Q$ gives $\Phi_Q(a)=\theta\circ a$ and $\Phi_Q^{-1}(b)=\psi\circ b$. Thus $\psi\theta=1_U$ and $\theta\psi=1_V$ by applying the inverse bijections to identities. This proves the claimed canonical isomorphism without an uncited representability assertion. To identify its standard evaluation construction, write $e:f^{-1}U\to H$ for the ordinary counit of step 1. Under the displayed bijections $1_U$ first becomes $e$, then $\operatorname{ev}_M\circ(e\otimes1_M)$, then $\epsilon^\times_K\circ Rf_!(\operatorname{ev}_M\circ(e\otimes1_M))$. Consequently $\theta$ is the tensor–Hom transpose of
$$U\otimes_A^LRf_!M\xrightarrow{\pi_{U,M}}Rf_!(f^{-1}U\otimes_A^LM)\xrightarrow{Rf_!(e\otimes1)}Rf_!(H\otimes_A^LM)\xrightarrow{Rf_!(\operatorname{ev}_M)}Rf_!f^\times K\xrightarrow{\epsilon^\times_K}K.$$
Here $\epsilon^\times$ is the exceptional counit of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. This formula also shows naturality in $M,K$ (contravariantly in $M$); alternatively it follows by evaluating the natural family $\Phi$ at identities.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a compactifiable morphism $f:X\to S$ between
Noetherian schemes, and arbitrary complexes $M$ on
$X$ and $K$ on $S$, there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K).
$$

proof.text:
For every test complex $Q$ on $S$, the ordinary
derived pullback, tensor, and internal-Hom adjunctions of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give

$$
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q,Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K))
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*Q\otimes_A^LM,f^\times K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Rf_!(f^*Q\otimes_A^LM),K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q\otimes_A^LRf_!M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Q,R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K)).
\end{split}
$$

The second bijection is
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]; the third is the
projection formula of
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], applied on a
compactification and preceded by exact extension by zero.
These bijections are natural in all three complexes.
Yoneda therefore gives the asserted canonical isomorphism.
It is the map obtained by applying $Rf_!$ to evaluation
and then composing with the counit, since the displayed
bijections transpose precisely those maps.
